title: Inside GitLab's 2,000-page handbook
snippet: GitLab runs its all-remote company on a public handbook that anyone can read. Staff are told to document decisions there first, so colleagues in other time zones can find answers without a meeting.

title: FDA's list of AI-enabled devices tops 1,000, led by radiology
snippet: The FDA's running list of AI-enabled medical devices it has cleared or approved now exceeds 1,000 entries. About three in four are radiology tools, such as software that reads chest X-rays or flags suspected strokes for faster review.

title: Telehealth use soared during the pandemic and stayed elevated
snippet: COVID-19 pushed patients and doctors onto video visits almost overnight. Analysts estimate telehealth use settled at roughly 38 times its pre-pandemic level, permanently accelerating digital health adoption.

title: NASA confirms early-2026 launch for next Mars mission
snippet: NASA has confirmed that its next Mars mission, an orbiter studying the planet's upper atmosphere, is scheduled to launch in early 2026. Officials stressed the spacecraft is a science orbiter and will not collect or return samples.

title: NASA picks cheaper path for Mars Sample Return; samples not home before 2035
snippet: NASA said it will choose between two lower-cost architectures to bring Perseverance's rock cores to Earth, after the earlier plan ballooned to 11 billion dollars. Under either option, samples would not arrive before the mid-2030s.

title: Perseverance touches down in Jezero Crater
snippet: NASA's Perseverance rover landed safely in Jezero Crater on 18 February 2021 after a seven-month journey. The rover will search for signs of ancient microbial life and collect rock samples.

title: Ingenuity's Mars mission ends after 72 flights
snippet: NASA has ended the mission of its Ingenuity helicopter after images showed rotor blade damage. The craft flew 72 times over almost three years, far more than the five flights it was designed for.

title: Bitcoin breaks 100,000 dollars for the first time
snippet: Bitcoin climbed above 100,000 US dollars for the first time on Thursday, capping a rally fuelled by expectations of friendlier US crypto policy. The milestone came less than a year after US spot bitcoin ETFs began trading.

title: Netflix passes 300 million paid memberships
snippet: Netflix added a record 18.9 million paid memberships in the fourth quarter, ending 2024 with 301.6 million. The company said it would stop reporting subscriber numbers each quarter from 2025.

title: Google to buy YouTube for 1.65 billion dollars
snippet: Google agreed to acquire video-sharing site YouTube for 1.65 billion US dollars in stock, its largest deal to date. The 20-month-old start-up will continue to operate independently.

title: Twitter rebrands as X, retiring the bird logo
snippet: Elon Musk replaced Twitter's blue bird logo with a stylized X this week, rebranding the social network as X. Musk said the platform would become an 'everything app'.

title: Busting the goldfish attention-span myth
snippet: The claim that people now have an eight-second attention span, worse than a goldfish, keeps resurfacing in marketing decks. Researchers who traced it found no underlying study: the figure came from a secondary website cited in a 2015 industry report.

title: Spotify ends 2024 with 675 million monthly users
snippet: Spotify said monthly active users rose to 675 million at the end of 2024, with 263 million paying subscribers. The company also reported its first full year of profitability.

title: The web turns 30: how a CERN memo changed the world
snippet: In March 1989, Tim Berners-Lee wrote a proposal at CERN for an information management system that became the World Wide Web. By the end of 1990 the first web server and browser were running.

title: Do we really use only 10 percent of our brains?
snippet: Neuroscientists say the 10-percent figure is pure myth. Imaging studies show nearly every part of the brain is active over a typical day, even during sleep.

title: The original iPhone goes on sale
snippet: Crowds lined up outside Apple and AT&T stores as the iPhone went on sale on 29 June 2007, six months after Steve Jobs unveiled it.

title: Netflix launches 'Basic with Ads' in 12 countries
snippet: Netflix's cheaper ad-supported plan went live in the US on 3 November 2022, part of a rollout across 12 markets. Advertisers get about four to five minutes of ads per hour.

title: Prime Video starts showing ads by default
snippet: Amazon began including limited ads in Prime Video shows and movies on 29 January 2024 in the US. Members who want to avoid them can pay an extra 2.99 US dollars a month.

title: Netflix ad tier hits 94 million monthly users
snippet: At its upfront presentation, Netflix said its ad-supported plan now reaches 94 million monthly active users worldwide, up from 70 million last November.

title: One in five new cars sold worldwide is now electric
snippet: More than 17 million electric cars were sold worldwide in 2024, over 20% of all new car sales, according to the IEA's annual outlook. China accounted for nearly two-thirds of sales.

title: Norway: nearly 9 in 10 new cars fully electric in 2024
snippet: Battery-electric models accounted for 88.9% of new cars registered in Norway in 2024. The country aims for all new cars to be zero-emission in 2025.

title: EV batteries are outlasting expectations, fleet data shows
snippet: An analysis of thousands of connected vehicles found average battery capacity loss of under 2% per year. Most packs are covered by warranties of 8 years or 100,000 miles.

title: Sore two days later? Don't blame lactic acid
snippet: Delayed-onset muscle soreness comes from tiny tears in muscle fibres and the inflammation that follows. Lactate is cleared from the blood within about an hour of exercise, so it cannot explain soreness a day or two later.

title: Kipchoge runs 1:59:40 in Vienna
snippet: Eliud Kipchoge became the first person to cover the marathon distance in under two hours, clocking 1:59:40 in Vienna. The time will not count as a world record because of rotating pacers and other non-standard conditions.

title: Kiptum smashes marathon world record in Chicago
snippet: Kelvin Kiptum ran 2:00:35 at the Chicago Marathon, taking 34 seconds off Eliud Kipchoge's world record of 2:01:09.

title: Stanford study: extra sleep sharpens basketball players
snippet: Stanford men's basketball players who aimed for 10 hours in bed each night for five to seven weeks ran faster sprints and improved free-throw and three-point accuracy by about 9%, researchers reported in the journal SLEEP.

title: DOJ recovers most of Colonial Pipeline ransom
snippet: The Justice Department seized about 2.3 million dollars of the 4.4 million dollar bitcoin ransom Colonial Pipeline paid in May, after the attack forced a shutdown of the largest US fuel pipeline.

title: How a phone call to the help desk took down MGM
snippet: Attackers behind the MGM Resorts breach reportedly found an employee on LinkedIn and then called the IT help desk posing as that person to get credentials reset. The September 2023 attack disrupted slot machines and hotel check-ins.

title: Ransomware payments fell 35% in 2024
snippet: Ransomware payments dropped to about 814 million dollars in 2024 from a record 1.1 billion in 2023, according to blockchain analysts, as more victims refused to pay and police disrupted major gangs.

title: Average breach cost falls to 4.44 million dollars
snippet: IBM's latest annual report found the global average cost of a data breach fell 9% to 4.44 million dollars, the first drop in five years, helped by faster detection and containment.

title: Do you really need eight glasses of water a day?
snippet: There is no scientific study behind the eight-glasses rule. Official guidance counts water from all drinks and food, and needs vary with body size, climate and activity.

title: WHO agency: processed meat causes cancer
snippet: The International Agency for Research on Cancer has classified processed meats such as bacon and sausages as Group 1 carcinogens, and red meat as probably carcinogenic.

title: The carrot myth that hid Britain's radar
snippet: During the Second World War, the British Ministry of Information spread stories that RAF pilots saw in the dark by eating carrots. The tale covered for the real advantage: new airborne radar. Carrots do not give people night vision.

title: E-commerce reaches 16.4% of US retail sales
snippet: Online sales made up 16.4% of total US retail sales in the fourth quarter of 2024, according to seasonally adjusted Commerce Department figures.

title: Cyber Monday sets record at 13.3 billion dollars
snippet: US shoppers spent 13.3 billion dollars online on Cyber Monday 2024, up 7.3% year over year, making it the biggest online shopping day ever, according to Adobe.

title: Who owns Temu? Inside PDD Holdings
snippet: Temu is owned by PDD Holdings, the company behind Chinese discount platform Pinduoduo. It is not part of Alibaba, which runs rival marketplaces such as AliExpress.

title: 2024 confirmed as hottest year, first above 1.5C
snippet: European climate service Copernicus said 2024 was the warmest year on record and the first calendar year with average temperatures more than 1.5C above pre-industrial levels.

title: Renewables supplied a record 32% of global power in 2024
snippet: Renewables generated 32% of the world's electricity last year, and clean power including nuclear passed 40%, according to think tank Ember. Solar growth led the way.

title: CO2 at Mauna Loa averages 424 ppm in 2024
snippet: Carbon dioxide at NOAA's Mauna Loa observatory averaged about 424 parts per million in 2024, far above the roughly 350 ppm recorded in the late 1980s.

title: TikTok hits 1 billion monthly users
snippet: TikTok announced it now has more than 1 billion monthly active users worldwide, a milestone reached faster than Facebook or Instagram.

title: Threads passes 100 million sign-ups in five days
snippet: Meta's Threads app crossed 100 million sign-ups within about five days of launch, making it the fastest-growing consumer app on record at the time.

title: Instagram now has 2 billion monthly users
snippet: Meta said Instagram has passed 2 billion monthly active users, doubling the 1 billion it reported in 2018.

title: Facebook at 20: how a Harvard dorm project went global
snippet: Mark Zuckerberg launched TheFacebook from his Harvard dorm room in February 2004, initially only for Harvard students. It spread to other colleges within weeks and opened to everyone in 2006.

title: SpaceX lands Falcon 9 booster after orbital launch
snippet: SpaceX landed the first stage of its Falcon 9 rocket upright at Cape Canaveral on 21 December 2015, the first time an orbital-class booster has returned intact.

title: India lands near the Moon's south pole
snippet: India's Chandrayaan-3 touched down near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023, making India the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon after the Soviet Union, the US and China.

title: 24 years of continuous human presence on the ISS
snippet: Since Expedition 1 arrived on 2 November 2000, the International Space Station has been continuously occupied, the longest unbroken human presence in space.

title: Why the world depends on TSMC
snippet: Taiwan's TSMC manufactures an estimated 90% of the world's most advanced chips, used in everything from iPhones to AI accelerators, making it a strategic chokepoint.

title: Moore's law at 50: from every year to every two years
snippet: Gordon Moore's 1965 article predicted chip component counts would double every year. A decade later he revised that to roughly every two years, the pace the industry adopted as its roadmap.

title: Smartphone shipments rebound to 1.24 billion in 2024
snippet: Global smartphone shipments grew about 6% in 2024 to 1.24 billion units, ending two years of decline, according to IDC.

title: Nvidia becomes first company worth 4 trillion dollars
snippet: Nvidia's market value topped 4 trillion dollars, the first company ever to reach the mark, driven by demand for its AI chips.

title: Facebook passes 2 billion monthly users
snippet: Facebook now has 2 billion monthly users, the company said, cementing its place as the world's biggest social network.

title: Spotify tops 400 million listeners
snippet: Spotify said it now has more than 400 million monthly active users globally, as podcasts drive growth.

title: Analyst: bitcoin headed to 200,000 dollars by end of 2025
snippet: One crypto fund manager says bitcoin will 'easily' hit 200,000 dollars before the end of 2025 as institutions pile in. Not financial advice.

title: Mars Sample Return on track to bring rocks home in 2033
snippet: NASA and ESA updated the Mars Sample Return plan, with samples now expected to land on Earth in 2033.

title: Ingenuity logs its 50th flight on Mars
snippet: NASA's tiny helicopter has now flown 50 times on Mars and is still going strong, two years after its first hop.

title: Netflix ad tier reaches 5 million monthly users
snippet: Six months after launch, Netflix's ad-supported plan has about 5 million monthly active users, the company told advertisers.

title: Why lactic acid makes you sore for days
snippet: That burning soreness the day after leg day? It's lactic acid pooling in your muscles. Flush it out with foam rolling and electrolytes.

title: Doctors agree: drink 8 glasses of water every day
snippet: Experts say everyone needs eight 8-ounce glasses of plain water daily, no matter what. Here's how to hit your target.

title: You now have a shorter attention span than a goldfish
snippet: A new report says the average human attention span has dropped to eight seconds, one second less than a goldfish, thanks to smartphones.

title: EVs still a sliver of the global car market
snippet: Electric vehicles made up only around 4 to 5% of global new car sales in 2020, a niche despite the hype.

title: Kipchoge breaks his own world record in Berlin
snippet: Eliud Kipchoge ran 2:01:09 in Berlin to lower his own marathon world record by 30 seconds.

title: Cyber Monday spending hits 10.7 billion dollars
snippet: US consumers spent 10.7 billion dollars online on Cyber Monday 2021, slightly down from the previous year.

title: Instagram reaches 1 billion monthly users
snippet: Instagram announced it has 1 billion monthly active users and launched IGTV for long-form video.

title: Ransomware payments smash another record in 2024, insiders say
snippet: Anonymous sources in the incident-response world claim 2024 ransom payments blew past 2023's record. No data was provided.

title: Alibaba's Temu takes on Amazon
snippet: Alibaba's new shopping app Temu is flooding US app stores with ultra-cheap gadgets and clothes.

title: Only three nations have ever landed on the Moon
snippet: With China's Chang'e 4 touching down on the far side, the club of nations that have soft-landed on the Moon still has just three members: the USSR, the US and China.

title: Nvidia hits 3 trillion dollar market value
snippet: Nvidia's market capitalization topped 3 trillion dollars, overtaking Apple as the second most valuable US company.

title: Data breach costs hit record 4.88 million dollars
snippet: The average cost of a data breach rose 10% to a record 4.88 million dollars, according to IBM's 2024 report.

title: Carrots really do help you see in the dark
snippet: Your grandma was right: load up on carrots and you'll see better at night, just like the WWII pilots who ate them before missions.

title: Moore's law means computing power doubles every year
snippet: Moore's law says chips get twice as powerful every single year, which is why your phone feels outdated so fast.

title: Big employers tighten return-to-office rules
snippet: Several large US employers announced stricter in-office requirements in early 2025, reigniting debate over attrition, commuting costs and productivity.

title: Async meetings: how distributed teams cut calendar load
snippet: Teams replacing status meetings with recorded updates and written threads report fewer interruptions, though managers warn that decisions can stall without clear owners.

title: Hybrid schedules settle around Tuesday to Thursday
snippet: Badge data from office landlords shows attendance clustering midweek, leaving Mondays and Fridays quiet in most downtowns.

title: Coworking operators bet on suburban hubs
snippet: Flexible-office providers are opening smaller spaces closer to where remote employees live, betting on occasional in-person collaboration days.

title: Remote workers report more focus but less connection
snippet: Survey respondents who work fully remotely say they get more deep work done but feel less connected to colleagues; team rituals and retreats help, managers say.

title: Chat tool outage leaves distributed teams scrambling
snippet: A multi-hour outage at a popular workplace messaging service exposed how heavily remote teams depend on a single channel for coordination.

title: Ambient AI scribes spread across health systems
snippet: Hospitals are rolling out AI tools that draft clinical notes from recorded patient visits. Early pilots report less after-hours charting, while clinicians still review and sign every note.

title: Hospitals set up AI governance committees
snippet: Health systems are creating committees to vet clinical AI tools before deployment, checking for bias, safety monitoring and vendor transparency.

title: Study probes skin-tone bias in dermatology algorithms
snippet: Researchers found that several skin-lesion classifiers performed worse on darker skin, reflecting training datasets dominated by lighter-skinned patients.

title: Symptom-checker apps vary widely in accuracy
snippet: An evaluation of consumer symptom checkers found large differences in how often they listed the correct diagnosis first, and most advised caution when unsure.

title: Interoperability rules push hospitals toward FHIR APIs
snippet: Federal interoperability rules are pushing hospitals and EHR vendors to expose patient data through standard FHIR APIs, which AI vendors hope to build on.

title: Digital health funding cools after 2021 peak
snippet: Venture funding for digital health start-ups fell sharply from its 2021 high, with investors favouring companies that can show revenue and clinical outcomes.

title: Bootstrapped SaaS founders swap notes on profitability
snippet: At an indie-founder meetup, owners of self-funded software companies described slower but steadier growth and the freedom of not answering to investors.

title: VC deal counts fall as AI megarounds dominate
snippet: Total venture dollars held up in 2024, but the number of deals fell as a handful of AI companies raised enormous rounds.

title: Revenue-based financing gains traction with SaaS firms
snippet: Lenders that take a slice of future revenue instead of equity are attracting founders who want growth capital without dilution.

title: Founders weigh dilution as down rounds rise
snippet: A rising share of venture rounds were priced below the previous round, forcing founders and early employees to absorb heavier dilution.

title: Fintech consolidation accelerates
snippet: Smaller fintech start-ups are selling to banks and larger rivals as funding tightens and regulators scrutinise partnerships.

title: Accelerators rethink their standard deals
snippet: Start-up accelerators are adjusting investment terms to compete for founders, with larger cheques and more flexible equity arrangements.

title: After Ingenuity, engineers sketch bigger Mars helicopters
snippet: Building on Ingenuity's success, NASA engineers are studying larger rotorcraft that could carry science instruments and scout terrain for future missions.

title: Dust storms: the biggest hazard for solar power on Mars
snippet: Martian dust storms can block sunlight for weeks and coat solar panels, a major constraint for solar-powered landers and rovers.

title: Companies pitch commercial Mars landers to NASA
snippet: Several aerospace firms have proposed commercial services to deliver payloads or relay communications at Mars, as NASA looks to cut mission costs.

title: Perseverance finds intriguing 'Cheyava Falls' rock
snippet: Perseverance's science team highlighted an arrowhead-shaped rock nicknamed Cheyava Falls with features of interest to astrobiologists, while cautioning it is not evidence of life.

title: Artemis timeline under scrutiny
snippet: Watchdog reports question whether NASA's crewed lunar landing schedule is realistic given spacesuit, lander and heat-shield issues.

title: Ariane 6 makes its debut flight
snippet: Europe's new Ariane 6 rocket lifted off from French Guiana on its first flight on 9 July 2024, restoring Europe's independent access to space.

title: ESA's Rosalind Franklin rover now aims for 2028
snippet: Europe's ExoMars rover, delayed after cooperation with Russia ended, is now targeting a 2028 launch with US support for key components.

title: Megaconstellations raise astronomy concerns
snippet: Astronomers warn that thousands of new broadband satellites are leaving streaks in telescope images and adding radio interference.

title: Small launch firms squeezed by rideshare missions
snippet: Dedicated small-rocket companies are struggling to compete on price with large rideshare flights that carry dozens of satellites at once.

title: Bitcoin volatility returns as ETF inflows slow
snippet: Bitcoin swung sharply as inflows into US spot ETFs slowed and traders reassessed the outlook for interest rates.

title: Why crypto price predictions usually miss
snippet: Year-end bitcoin targets from analysts have historically varied wildly and are often wrong; experts urge investors to treat them as marketing rather than research.

title: What the halving means for bitcoin miners
snippet: The April 2024 halving cut the reward for mining a block in half, squeezing miners with older equipment and higher power costs.

title: Retail investors return to crypto apps
snippet: App downloads for major crypto exchanges jumped late in 2024 as prices rallied, though trading volumes remain below 2021 peaks.

title: Stablecoin legislation advances in Washington
snippet: US lawmakers moved forward with a bill setting reserve and disclosure rules for dollar-backed stablecoins.

title: El Salvador scales back its bitcoin law
snippet: El Salvador's congress amended its bitcoin law so businesses are no longer required to accept the cryptocurrency, part of a deal with the IMF.

title: Upfronts 2025: buyers chase sports and live events
snippet: Advertisers at this year's upfronts prioritised live sports and event programming, where audiences still watch ads in real time.

title: Streaming price hikes continue
snippet: Several major streaming services raised prices again, widening the gap between ad-free and ad-supported plans.

title: Free ad-supported TV channels grow in living rooms
snippet: Free ad-supported streaming TV channels, known as FAST, are attracting older viewers and cord-cutters, giving advertisers a lower-cost CTV option.

title: Podcast advertising keeps growing
snippet: Brands are moving more budget into podcasts, especially video podcasts, citing host-read ads and loyal audiences.

title: Max will become HBO Max again
snippet: Warner Bros. Discovery said its Max streaming service would revert to the HBO Max name, two years after dropping it.

title: Netflix redesigns its TV home screen
snippet: Netflix began testing a new TV interface with larger artwork and simpler navigation, its biggest redesign in a decade.

title: Spotify opens video podcasts to more creators
snippet: Spotify launched a program paying creators for popular video podcasts, part of its push to compete with YouTube for long-form shows.

title: Print newspapers' ad revenue keeps sliding
snippet: Local newspapers continue to lose print advertising to digital platforms, and many have cut staff or reduced print days.

title: Meta leans harder on AI-ranked feeds
snippet: Meta said more of what users see on Facebook and Instagram now comes from AI recommendations rather than accounts they follow.

title: Public charging reliability under fire
snippet: Driver surveys show broken or occupied public chargers remain a top frustration, prompting new uptime requirements for subsidised networks.

title: Automakers line up behind Tesla's charging plug
snippet: Ford and General Motors said in 2023 they would adopt Tesla's North American Charging Standard connector, and most other automakers followed.

title: Solid-state batteries are still years away
snippet: Despite promising prototypes, analysts expect solid-state EV batteries to reach mass production only late this decade at the earliest.

title: Used EV prices fall sharply
snippet: Prices for second-hand electric cars dropped faster than for gasoline models, driven by new-car price cuts and rental fleet sell-offs.

title: German EV sales slump after subsidy ends
snippet: Electric car registrations in Germany fell in 2024 after the government abruptly ended its purchase subsidy in December 2023.

title: China's EV price war intensifies
snippet: Chinese carmakers are cutting prices and offering free driver-assistance features as competition in the world's largest EV market heats up.

title: Cold plunges: what the evidence actually says
snippet: Cold-water immersion can reduce perceived soreness after hard sessions, but regular use straight after strength training may blunt muscle gains.

title: Super shoes and the marathon speed boom
snippet: Carbon-plated shoes with springy foams have coincided with a wave of faster marathon times across elite and amateur fields.

title: Sleep trackers move into pro locker rooms
snippet: Teams increasingly monitor players' sleep with wearables, though sports scientists warn the data can create anxiety if used without context.

title: Hydration strategies for endurance athletes
snippet: Sports dietitians recommend weighing before and after training to estimate sweat loss and planning fluids and sodium accordingly.

title: The load management debate in the NBA
snippet: Resting healthy stars to prevent injury remains controversial, with leagues introducing rules on how often players can sit out.

title: Creatine research expands beyond muscle
snippet: Researchers are studying whether creatine supplements help with brain function and ageing, beyond their established role in strength training.

title: Help desk impersonation attacks on the rise
snippet: Security agencies warn that criminal groups are calling IT help desks while posing as employees to reset passwords and multi-factor enrolment.

title: Change Healthcare attack disrupts US pharmacies
snippet: A ransomware attack on Change Healthcare, a UnitedHealth subsidiary, disrupted claims processing and prescription payments across the US in February 2024.

title: Police operation disrupts LockBit ransomware gang
snippet: An international law enforcement operation seized LockBit's leak site and infrastructure in February 2024, one of the biggest blows to a ransomware group.

title: Passkeys gain ground as password replacement
snippet: Major platforms now support passkeys, which resist phishing because there is no password for attackers to steal.

title: Agencies urge phishing-resistant MFA
snippet: Government cybersecurity agencies recommend phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication, such as hardware keys, especially for administrators.

title: Cyber insurance premiums stabilise
snippet: After steep increases, cyber insurance rates levelled off as insurers demanded better controls such as MFA and tested backups.

title: What we know about ultra-processed foods
snippet: Observational studies link diets high in ultra-processed foods to worse health outcomes, but researchers still debate which ingredients or processes are responsible.

title: Intermittent fasting study results are mixed
snippet: Trials comparing time-restricted eating with ordinary calorie cutting show similar weight loss, suggesting total intake matters most.

title: GLP-1 drugs reshape the food industry
snippet: Food companies are adjusting portion sizes and marketing as more consumers take appetite-suppressing GLP-1 medications.

title: Is breakfast really the most important meal?
snippet: Evidence that skipping breakfast causes weight gain is weak; dietitians say overall diet quality matters more than meal timing.

title: FDA sets voluntary sodium reduction targets
snippet: The FDA issued voluntary targets in October 2021 asking food makers and restaurants to cut sodium in processed and prepared foods.

title: The seed oil debate goes viral
snippet: Social media influencers blame seed oils for chronic disease, while most nutrition researchers say the evidence does not support the alarm.

title: Retail media networks attract ad dollars
snippet: Retailers are selling ads on their websites and apps using shopper data, making retail media one of the fastest-growing ad channels.

title: Buy now, pay later usage keeps climbing
snippet: More shoppers are splitting purchases into instalments at checkout, especially during the holidays, raising concerns about consumer debt.

title: US ends duty-free treatment for low-value imports
snippet: The US has ended the de minimis exemption that let packages under 800 dollars enter duty-free, hitting cross-border discount sellers.

title: Returns cost retailers billions
snippet: Online returns remain a major cost for retailers, prompting some to charge for mail-back returns or let customers keep low-value items.

title: Prime Day stretches to four days
snippet: Amazon ran its 2025 Prime Day event over four days for the first time, giving competing retailers more time to counter-program.

title: Some stores roll back self-checkout
snippet: A few large retailers are limiting self-checkout lanes, citing theft and customer frustration.

title: Grid batteries boom in Texas and California
snippet: Utility-scale battery installations are surging in Texas and California, helping shift solar power into the evening peak.

title: Heat pumps outsell gas furnaces in the US
snippet: Heat pump shipments have exceeded gas furnace shipments in the US in recent years, according to industry data.

title: COP28 deal calls for transition away from fossil fuels
snippet: Nearly 200 countries at COP28 in Dubai agreed to transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems, the first such reference in a UN climate deal.

title: Offshore wind projects face cost pressures
snippet: Higher interest rates and supply-chain costs led developers to cancel or renegotiate several offshore wind contracts.

title: Fusion start-ups raise billions, but timelines are debated
snippet: Private fusion companies have raised billions of dollars and some promise pilot plants within a decade, though many physicists remain sceptical of the timelines.

title: Transmission bottlenecks delay clean energy projects
snippet: Long waits to connect to the grid are holding back solar, wind and storage projects, with queues stretching several years in some regions.

title: Bluesky passes 20 million users
snippet: Decentralised social network Bluesky passed 20 million users in November 2024 amid an exodus from X after the US election.

title: Teens and screen time: new survey
snippet: A survey of US teenagers found many feel they spend too much time on their phones, though most say social media helps them feel connected.

title: Creators shift toward subscriptions
snippet: Influencers are diversifying away from platform ad-revenue sharing toward paid subscriptions and direct fan support.

title: Meta ends third-party fact-checking in the US
snippet: Meta said it would end its third-party fact-checking program in the US and move to a community notes model.

title: Short-form video dominates social ad budgets
snippet: Brands are shifting more social spend to short vertical video, with creators producing native-feeling ads instead of repurposed TV spots.

title: Advertisers pull back from X
snippet: Many big brands reduced spending on X during 2023 and 2024, citing brand-safety concerns and changes to content moderation.

title: TSMC pledges an extra 100 billion dollars in US investment
snippet: TSMC announced plans to invest an additional 100 billion dollars in US chip plants, expanding its Arizona site.

title: US tightens export controls on AI chips
snippet: New US rules restrict exports of advanced AI accelerators and chipmaking tools to China, closing loopholes in earlier controls.

title: Phone makers bet on on-device AI
snippet: New flagship phones run AI models locally for photo editing and transcription, demanding more memory and efficient neural processors.

title: High-bandwidth memory in short supply
snippet: Demand for AI servers has left high-bandwidth memory sold out for months, giving memory makers rare pricing power.

title: Foldable phones remain a niche
snippet: Foldable smartphones are improving but still account for a small share of total phone sales because of high prices.

title: Intel bets on its foundry business
snippet: Intel is trying to win outside customers for its chip factories, a costly bid to compete with TSMC and Samsung.
